message.content:
In Blackjack, an Ace is a “flexible” card: it can be counted as either **1** or **11**, depending on which value gives your hand the best chance of winning without busting.

Key points:

| Situation | How the Ace is treated |
|-----------|------------------------|
| **Initial hand** | If you’re dealt an Ace plus a 10‑value card (10, J, Q, K), that’s a *natural* Blackjack (21). |
| **Adding cards** | After the initial deal, you may choose to hit or stand. If adding a card would cause your total to exceed 21, you can “downgrade” an Ace from 11 to 1 to avoid busting. |
| **Multiple Aces** | With two Aces, the hand is normally valued at 12 (one Ace as 11, the other as 1). If you hit and receive another Ace, you can adjust the values again (e.g., three Aces could be 13 or 14, etc.). |
| **Splitting** | If you’re dealt two Aces, you can split them into two separate hands. Most casinos allow you to hit each new hand once (or not at all) after splitting Aces, but you can’t “double down” on a split Ace in many rulesets. |

So the core rule: **An Ace can be worth 1 or 11, whichever keeps the hand from busting and gives the highest possible total ≤ 21.**
